Pane tunnel lining and seal. The grey tunnel reads as in tt_window, with its 3-step grade toward the pane. At extreme obliquity (s01 left edge) the lining dominates, which is plausible.

Electric shades. The pleat count is right: 30 over the opening in b_jClose by FFT, against 33 in omaat_room24. The blackout tone is now slightly pale (0.675 of the wall against 0.57). Pleat contrast is half the photo's: L std 22.5 on a mean of 160 (cv 0.14) against 39 on 113 (cv 0.33). The photo's blackout has crisp dark valley lines, while ours is a soft grey corduroy. Mid-distance moire persists (s05). The sheer (b_jSheer) and the LED colour are right.
Manual PY/Y shades: open with grip band, half and closed (s08, studio win_front/win_low). Unchanged and reads right against sp_py24.

Dado, air-return grilles and placards. b_dadoY2 is now framed on the window and shows no dado, so the close-up is not checkable. In s07 the dado is (72,77,89), 0.375 of the wall (py_37303 0.44; this spot is shadowed by the door), slate B-R +17, grille (37,40,48). The studio win_low layout is unchanged and right.

Carpets. The Y aisle is (45,54,76) in ra_carpetY and (44,54,76) in q16, against y_47303 (36,42,67): right navy, a touch lifted. The J aisle in q06 is a plausible brown. The door-bay carpet is (71,61,51), matching sans_09's door-2 bay, while lalf_134 (door 3) is a neutral charcoal (74,69,70).
Door / galley vinyl. The cloudy mottle reads at low frequency. It is faintly cool and lavender (105,104,110) and lacks the fine speckle (L std 12.6 against sans_09 ~24).

Type A door surround and viewing window. The arc, handle housing, assist bar with red strap, EXIT sign and slide-bar placard all read like lalf_134. The window is correctly forward of the grip, beside the arrowhead (b_doorWin, s06, s07, and mirrored in q21). It is still narrow (~0.43 aspect against >=0.53), with a dark grey seal instead of the photo's bright cream bezel, and has no shade tab. The lining is neutral (B/R 0.98 against 0.93).

issues.detail: Blackout pleats: weak near contrast and mid-distance moire, from the same cause
issues.problem: The pleat stripe is per-vertex colour on alternate rows (07_shell.js l.425-426, kf 0.62). Near, the contrast is cv 0.14 against 0.33 in omaat_room24, so the photo's crisp dark valley lines become a soft corduroy. Far, the stripe cannot mip-filter and beats against the pixel grid (s05, windows 3-4). Raising kf to fix one worsens the other. This has persisted 4 rounds on a hero element (every J/F window when closed).
issues.evidence: b_jClose col 300: std 22.5 / mean 160. omaat_room24 col 620: std 39 / mean 113, period 25 px, 33 pleats. ra12/z_s05_far.png shows wavy beat bands.
issues.fix: Move the stripe out of vertex colour into a mip-mapped detail layer on uv.v (u already runs 0..1 along the rows, k/n in g.u l.416): 31 cycles per shade, a valley line ~25% of the period at x0.55, crest x1.0. Mipmaps then average distant shades to flat taupe, so kf can effectively go to cv ~0.3 near. Delete the l.426 loop. If a new layer is not allowed in shared 03_tex.js: keep the vertex stripe but make it 1 row dark / 3 rows light with n = 124 (sharper valley line), and add a far-LOD shade instance with no stripe beyond ~4 m in shadeMats.

issues.detail: [lighting] Cream finishes render dead neutral: bowls, bezels, door lining, sidewall
issues.problem: Every recess surface is s 0.004-0.005 (221,221,220), against omaat_room24 s 0.13 (201,193,175) and tt_window s 0.23. The door lining is B/R 0.98 against lalf_134 0.93. The albedos are cream (#ece4d5, #e4dccb), so the pipeline removes about 95% of the saturation. This is now the largest single gap against the real photos and is visible at every distance. It is not scored against the shell.
